 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 01.06.2023 at about 07.45 a.m, the petitioner was going for his work by riding a Motor (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.6765/2023 Cycle bearing No.KA-04-JG-0511 on Dasarahalli Lake Road from Dasarahalli Signal towards NTTF Junction, when he reached the Dainametic Junction, at that time one Etios Cab bearing No.KA-51-C-9678 driven by its driver, in rash and negligent manner, came at high speed from left side of the road from System Bus Stand side and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and two-wheeler also got repaired.

Immediately after the accident,
the petitioner was shifted to Raghavendra People Tree hospital, wherein after first aid treatment, for further treatment he was shifted to Aryan Multi Speciality hospital,
Jnanaganganagara, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and X-rays were taken and fractures were noted and was operated and implants were fixed and discharged on 04.06.2023 with an advise to complete bed rest for a period of 3 to 4 months and accordingly he has taken follow-up treatment and medication and he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment, food,
transport and other charges.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES

01. Whether the petitioner is proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 01.06.2023 at about 07.45 a.m, at Dynametic Junction Lake Road, T.Dasarahalli, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of Etios Car bearing registration No.KA-51-C-9678 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03

. What Order or Award?
06.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined him as PW.1 and got examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Executive Officer as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.

08. Heard both sides.
09.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1

sentences.text: Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though he has been (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.6765/2023 elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Cab by its driver, the accident took place and petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Peenya Traffic Police against driver of the offending cab.
Ex.P.2 is Complaint shows due to rash and negligent driving of the offending cab the accident was occurred and due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
Ex.P.3 is Police intimation wherein it is mentioned that "Alleged H/O RTA, hit by four wheeler (Cab) to two-wheeler (Bike) passenger @ Dynamic Circle, Dasarahalli, on 01.06.2023 at 07.45 a.m".
Ex.P.4 is Wound certificate which shows that petitioner sustained Fracture left ankle and doctor has opined that said injury is grievous in nature.
Ex.P.5 is original Discharge summary shows that the petitioner sustained Bimalleolar fracture left ankle.

Ex.P.8 is Charge sheet shows after completion of investigation, the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of Etios Cab for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of IPC and U/Sec 134(B) and 187 of IMV Act.

Ex.P.9 and 10 are Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.6765/2023 the place of accident on NTTF Signal and T.Dasarahalli Signal Road, near Dynamatic Factory Junction,
Bengaluru, which is not disputed.

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Etios Cab.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
This Issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 44 years and was working as Production In-charge in J.L. Multi Tech,
Tavarekere, Bengaluru and was earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m and he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment, food, transport and other charges.
On account of the accidental injuries, he could not attend to his work and lost his earnings and has become permanent disabled.

12. It is the duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.6765/2023 certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.7 Aadhaar card.

Even though said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 30.11.1978 and the alleged accident was occurred on 01.06.2023.

Therefore,
considering the said document, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 45 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.

sentences.text: With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, except Ex.P.6 Salary certificate issued by J.L. Multi Tech, Bengaluru, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal or not examined the author of said document or employer of said organization.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.6765/2023 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,000/- and it is multiplied by 12.
14.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner sustained bi-malleolar fracture left ankle and he has assessed physical disability of left lower limbs at 36% and to the whole body at 12%
and he has produced Clinical report and X-ray as per Ex.P.14 and 15.
In his cross-examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally.
He has not seen the follow-up records, case sheet and old X-rays and he has not taken opinion from the treated doctor.
Presently fracture is united and implants are removed.

With difficulty petitioner can perform his day to day activities and also supervise work and admits that petitioner not complained to the treated doctor about complainants mentioned in para 5 and 6 and denied to the suggestion that petitioner not suffered any kind of disability.

However, considering the evidence of PW.2, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.6765/2023 disability of the petitioner at 12%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.16,000/- x 12 x 14 x 12%/100 = Rs.3,22,560/-.
15.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Discharge summary of Aryan Multi Speciality hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for 04 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore,
considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

16. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.4 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and as per Clinical report, X-rays and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to fractures suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
17. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.6765/2023 income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,000/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 04 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least two months.
Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/- (Rs.16,000 x 2) under this head.

sentences.text: Medical expenses:- The petitioner has produced original Inpatient bill for Rs.68,314/- and entire Medical bills as per Ex.P.11 and 12 for Rs.23,549/-.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent No.2 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.91,863/- under this head.

19. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.
Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1. Loss of future income 3,22,560-00 2.
Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00 3.
Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and conveyance  charges 4.
Medical Expenses 91,863-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00  unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 33,000-00  period  Total 5,37,423-00 21.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,37,423/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

22. Regarding liability:- To disprove the case of the petitioner, the respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Executive Officer as RW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the objections averments therein and in her cross-examination she stated that she has deposed based on the Police documents and she has produced (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.6765/2023 Authorization letter and copy of Policy as per Ex.R.1 and 2 which shows that the insurance policy to the offending Etios Cab is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

23. Issue No.3:- In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
